breaks.Break_Summary: Enterprise breadth becomes economically/operationally irrational for a low-complexity or speed-first buyer.
breaks.Build_or_Config_Implication: Reduce modules, integrations, custom flows and governance surface; validate a bounded implementation.
breaks.Buyer_Question: Show the minimum viable Genesys architecture, services effort and three-year TCO for our actual scope-not the full platform.
breaks.Change_Consequence: Each new module/integration adds regression and ownership cost.
breaks.Cost_Consequence: Higher implementation/admin cost relative to utilized value.
breaks.Day2_Consequence: Underutilization, admin overhead and slower change.
breaks.Exit_Point: Eliminate Genesys if the minimum rational design still requires materially more implementation, administration or commercial commitment than the buyer can use.
breaks.Mitigation_Method: Right-size to a lower CX tier and narrow scope; if transformation overhead still exceeds value, select a simpler architecture.
breaks.Refresh_Trigger: Material pricing, architecture, quota, BPO feature, release/deprecation or AI lifecycle change.
breaks.Trigger_Condition: Buyer needs standard inbound/digital service with limited WEM/AI/integration complexity and lacks a mature platform operating team.

breaks.Break_Summary: Peak routing or outbound demand exceeds documented quotas/headroom and required increases cannot be proven in the implementation window.
breaks.Build_or_Config_Implication: Capacity model, queue behavior, CPS, campaign concurrency and upstream carrier throughput must be tested end to end.
breaks.Buyer_Question: Prove our P95/P99 and peak-event workload against current org limits, increase process, carrier capacity and failure behavior.
breaks.Change_Consequence: Growth or channel mix changes can invalidate prior headroom.
breaks.Cost_Consequence: Potential capacity engineering, carrier and test cost; missed peaks create revenue/CX impact.
breaks.Day2_Consequence: Queue delay or throughput constraint during demand spikes.
breaks.Exit_Point: Eliminate or redesign if mandatory peak throughput cannot be demonstrated with approved limits and end-to-end capacity.
breaks.Mitigation_Method: Pre-size the workload, request quota/CPS increases early, load test, and redesign queue/campaign architecture where needed.
breaks.Refresh_Trigger: Material pricing, architecture, quota, BPO feature, release/deprecation or AI lifecycle change.
breaks.Trigger_Condition: Extreme surge, seasonal spikes or high-CPS outbound programs materially exceed default service limits.

breaks.Break_Summary: BPO or multi-brand client isolation cannot be satisfied safely through the proposed single-org/division model, while multi-org administration is operationally unacceptable.
breaks.Build_or_Config_Implication: Org topology, identities, routing, reporting, WEM, recordings, integrations and shared services must be separated and tested.
breaks.Buyer_Question: Demonstrate hard client isolation and an efficient shared-agent/admin workflow across representative client organizations.
breaks.Change_Consequence: Adding clients multiplies change and admin surface unless templated.
breaks.Cost_Consequence: Additional org/admin/licensing/integration overhead; possible margin impact.
breaks.Day2_Consequence: Multi-org context switching, duplicated configuration or reporting burden.
breaks.Exit_Point: Eliminate the proposed topology if contractual isolation or required shared-agent economics cannot be proven.
breaks.Mitigation_Method: Use separate organizations, authorized-organization access and explicit shared-service design; prove operator workflows and per-client controls.
breaks.Refresh_Trigger: Material pricing, architecture, quota, BPO feature, release/deprecation or AI lifecycle change.
breaks.Trigger_Condition: Buyer needs hard regulatory/data separation across clients plus efficient shared-agent/admin operations.

breaks.Affected_Buyer_or_Use_Case: AI-heavy, high-volume or highly integrated buyers
breaks.Break_Summary: Consumption layers make the total cost materially higher or less predictable than the buyer's approved economic envelope.
breaks.Build_or_Config_Implication: Create a workload-to-license/usage model and instrumentation before production.
breaks.Buyer_Question: Show our expected monthly charges under baseline, peak and growth scenarios using the exact contracted rates and allowances.
breaks.Change_Consequence: New AI use cases or channel growth can raise consumption quickly.
breaks.Cost_Consequence: Overage and AI-token spend; potential budget variance.
breaks.Day2_Consequence: Ongoing usage monitoring and optimization required.
breaks.Exit_Point: Eliminate or re-scope if three-year TCO remains outside the economic envelope after negotiated protections.
breaks.Mitigation_Method: Model usage by feature, prepay/cap where sensible, monitor consumption and negotiate renewal/overage protections.
breaks.Refresh_Trigger: Material pricing, architecture, quota, BPO feature, release/deprecation or AI lifecycle change.
breaks.Trigger_Condition: High API/BYOC/storage/transcription/AI usage, seasonal volatility or rapid AI adoption exceeds included allowances.

breaks.Break_Summary: A heavily customized Genesys estate becomes difficult to operate or change because weekly platform evolution, API/integration deprecations and AI model transitions outpace the buyer's regression capacity.
breaks.Build_or_Config_Implication: Inventory APIs/integrations/models; build test automation and documented rollback/fallback.
breaks.Buyer_Question: Show the active deprecation exposure in our proposed design and demonstrate how changes are detected, tested, promoted and rolled back.
breaks.Change_Consequence: Every dependency increases the cost of future platform/model changes.
breaks.Cost_Consequence: Persistent engineering labor plus migration work for deprecated dependencies.
breaks.Day2_Consequence: Release review and regression become permanent operating work.
breaks.Exit_Point: Eliminate or simplify the architecture if the buyer cannot sustain the required change-management cadence.
breaks.Mitigation_Method: Reduce bespoke dependencies, maintain regression suites, monitor announcements, assign owners and contract support/transition obligations.
breaks.Refresh_Trigger: Material pricing, architecture, quota, BPO feature, release/deprecation or AI lifecycle change.
breaks.Trigger_Condition: Buyer depends on many custom APIs, embedded clients, legacy integration methods or sensitive AI workflows but has weak release engineering.

implementation.AI_Work: Moderate-to-high: AI model/provider mapping, knowledge, guardrails, tools/actions, evaluation, token economics and release/model lifecycle controls must be productionized.
implementation.Architecture_Work: Moderate for standard single-region patterns; High for multi-region/global, sovereignty-sensitive, high-volume, multi-org BPO and co-built CRM/service architectures.
implementation.Discovery_Complexity: Moderate-to-high: discovery must resolve license tier, regions/data paths, telephony/carrier, queue/routing/Architect topology, WEM org design, integrations, migration/coexistence, AI authority/knowledge, consumption economics and Day-2 ownership.
implementation.Estimated_Timeline_Band: CONTEXT-DEPENDENT; no defensible universal enterprise duration is supported by public evidence.
implementation.External_Services_Dependency: Scope-dependent. Genesys/partners/SIs can be material for complex migrations, global telephony, custom integrations and AI; routine administration can move in-house after enablement.
implementation.Gravity_Rationale: MODERATE for bounded deployments using standard voice/digital/routing and packaged integrations; HIGH for typical large-enterprise transformations spanning global telephony, digital, WEM, CRM/service workflows, migration/coexistence and AI; can become TRANSFORMATIONAL when heavy custom integration, multi-region sovereignty, BPO multi-org or agentic AI are combined.
implementation.Integration_Work: Low-to-moderate for standard AppFoundry/co-built patterns; High for custom APIs, data actions, BYOI and multi-system orchestration.
implementation.Key_Assumptions: Gravity is driven by scope, incumbent complexity, number of regions/carriers/integrations, WEM redesign, AI authority, BPO topology and buyer operating maturity.
implementation.Migration_Work: Moderate-to-high depending on incumbent telephony, numbers, flows, recordings/history, integrations and coexistence; BYOI can reduce big-bang pressure but adds data-connector responsibility.
implementation.PMO_Need: High for multi-workstream enterprise/global transformations; lower for bounded departmental deployments.
implementation.Porting_Cutover: Moderate-to-high where numbers/carriers, legacy PBX/CC, global sites or staged coexistence are involved.
implementation.Routing_IVR_Work: Moderate for standard Architect/queue configuration; High for complex predictive routing, work automation, cross-department orchestration and large legacy flow conversion.
implementation.Testing_UAT: High for enterprise scope: routing/capacity, carrier failover, outbound CPS, WFM scale, CRM/workflow failures, data integrity, AI action/recovery, reporting, security and cutover must be tested.
implementation.Training_Change_Management: Moderate-to-high across admins, supervisors, WEM teams, developers, security, AI/knowledge owners and frontline users.

sow_exposure.Acceptance_Criterion: Pilot and production cutover prove inbound/outbound, emergency-service requirements, failover and rollback by country.
sow_exposure.Customer_Responsibility: Provide authoritative number inventory, carrier contracts, locations, regulatory requirements and freeze windows.
sow_exposure.Required_SOW_Language: Inventory every country/number range, carrier model, porting dependency, emergency calling requirement, SBC/BYOC ownership, failover path and cutover rollback.
sow_exposure.Typical_Assumption_or_Exclusion: Genesys Cloud Voice, BYOC and local numbering/carrier choices are not assumed to have identical country coverage, lead times, emergency-services treatment or failover behavior.
sow_exposure.Vendor_or_SI_Responsibility: Genesys/SI validates supported carrier architecture, porting plan, failover, lead times and support RACI.

sow_exposure.Acceptance_Criterion: Buyer-controlled UAT proves golden paths, exceptions, transfers, callbacks, overflow and degraded modes against agreed cases.
sow_exposure.Customer_Responsibility: Provide current flows, queue/skill definitions, business rules and SMEs; approve rationalization decisions.
sow_exposure.Required_SOW_Language: Define source-flow inventory, decision logic, exception paths, reusable components, object ownership, acceptance scenarios and out-of-scope redesign.
sow_exposure.Typical_Assumption_or_Exclusion: Legacy routing/IVR logic is assumed to be fully documented and directly portable; hidden business rules, exceptions or queue behavior can expand design scope.
sow_exposure.Vendor_or_SI_Responsibility: Genesys/SI maps current-to-target flows, identifies redesign, builds/configures in-scope logic and documents admin ownership.

sow_exposure.Acceptance_Criterion: Load/scale test reaches buyer-defined peak plus headroom without queueing, throttling or limit-induced failure outside agreed thresholds.
sow_exposure.Customer_Responsibility: Provide peak/burst history, event calendar, staffing, outbound plan and growth assumptions.
sow_exposure.Required_SOW_Language: State peak interaction/contact/agent-evaluation assumptions, outbound campaign counts/CPS, WFM organizational limits, required headroom, quota-increase owner and deadline.
sow_exposure.Typical_Assumption_or_Exclusion: Cloud elasticity is assumed to remove the need for application-level capacity planning, quota validation or increase lead time.
sow_exposure.Vendor_or_SI_Responsibility: Genesys/SI validates documented limits against the design, files required increases and demonstrates monitoring/headroom.

sow_exposure.Acceptance_Criterion: Production-like tests prove context, routing, action/write-back, failure behavior and recovery across both platforms.
sow_exposure.Customer_Responsibility: Provide CRM/ITSM data model, identity architecture, sandbox access, workflow owners and target experience.
sow_exposure.Required_SOW_Language: Name exact product/SKU, routing owner, data objects, screen-pop/write-back/actions, identity, environment mapping, support owner, release dependencies and acceptance tests.
sow_exposure.Typical_Assumption_or_Exclusion: A co-built integration is assumed to eliminate configuration, data-model, routing-ownership, version and incident-boundary work.
sow_exposure.Vendor_or_SI_Responsibility: Genesys/SI plus CRM/ITSM owner configures supported integration and documents joint incident escalation and change control.

sow_exposure.Acceptance_Criterion: Failure injection proves timeout, retry, duplicate prevention, degraded behavior, alerting and recovery without customer-state corruption.
sow_exposure.Customer_Responsibility: Provide target-system APIs, credentials, limits, test environments and business owners.
sow_exposure.Required_SOW_Language: Inventory every custom/API/AppFoundry dependency; define authentication, rate limits, retry/idempotency, source ownership, observability, support RACI, versioning and retirement handling.
sow_exposure.Typical_Assumption_or_Exclusion: Public APIs and marketplace breadth are assumed to make custom integrations low-effort and vendor-supported regardless of design.
sow_exposure.Vendor_or_SI_Responsibility: Builder owns code/config quality; Genesys supports documented platform behavior; third party owns its product unless explicitly contracted otherwise.

sow_exposure.Acceptance_Criterion: Parallel-run comparison meets agreed event, routing, reporting and WEM accuracy thresholds before legacy retirement.
sow_exposure.Customer_Responsibility: Provide incumbent extracts/interfaces, mapping rules and validated baseline reports.
sow_exposure.Required_SOW_Language: Define interaction/data sources, mapping, presence/routing ownership, coexistence period, historical-data treatment, reconciliation, cutover gates and retirement criteria.
sow_exposure.Typical_Assumption_or_Exclusion: Historical interactions, routing context, WEM data and reporting semantics are assumed to remain equivalent during coexistence/migration.
sow_exposure.Vendor_or_SI_Responsibility: Genesys/SI configures BYOI/migration components in scope and discloses customer/partner connector responsibilities.

sow_exposure.Acceptance_Criterion: Forecast/schedule/QM tests prove scale, permissions, reporting and exception handling for agreed peak organization.
sow_exposure.Customer_Responsibility: Provide workforce hierarchy, demand history, schedules, QA forms, exception policies and growth forecast.
sow_exposure.Required_SOW_Language: Define business units, management units, agents, route groups, queues, offered-interaction volumes, async work, forecast history, QA forms and cross-unit ownership.
sow_exposure.Typical_Assumption_or_Exclusion: Current workforce hierarchy, staffing model and QA program are assumed to map cleanly without hitting management-unit/business-unit limits or redesigning operations.
sow_exposure.Vendor_or_SI_Responsibility: Genesys/SI validates design against documented WFM limits and configures in-scope WEM objects; buyer owns policy and operational sign-off.

sow_exposure.Acceptance_Criterion: Blind test set proves answer/action integrity, refusal/escalation, permission boundaries, recovery and cost thresholds before production authority.
sow_exposure.Customer_Responsibility: Provide governed knowledge, policies, action APIs, gold-set cases, risk owners and cost envelope.
sow_exposure.Required_SOW_Language: Define AI use cases, model/provider dependency, knowledge sources, tool/action permissions, human approval, guardrails, evaluation set, rollback/kill path, token budget and lifecycle/revalidation.
sow_exposure.Typical_Assumption_or_Exclusion: AI features are assumed to be plug-and-play with stable model behavior, complete knowledge, safe action authority and predictable token cost.
sow_exposure.Vendor_or_SI_Responsibility: Genesys/SI configures supported AI components; buyer owns domain policy/approval; model/tool owners share runtime responsibility.

sow_exposure.Acceptance_Criterion: Security/privacy review signs off feature-level data flow and control matrix; exceptions are contractually documented.
sow_exposure.Customer_Responsibility: Provide regulatory/data-classification requirements, retention rules and approved geographies.
sow_exposure.Required_SOW_Language: Map data classes and processing locations by feature; identify subprocessors, satellite media, recordings/transcripts, keys, exports, retention and customer responsibilities.
sow_exposure.Typical_Assumption_or_Exclusion: Selecting a core region is assumed to prove every feature, AI subprocess, recording path, integration and support operation stays within the same residency boundary.
sow_exposure.Vendor_or_SI_Responsibility: Genesys supplies current region/subprocessor/control evidence; SI/buyer validates enabled-feature data paths and configuration.

sow_exposure.Acceptance_Criterion: All mandatory scenarios pass with documented evidence and no open defect above agreed severity threshold.
sow_exposure.Customer_Responsibility: Provide test data, SMEs, load profile, test numbers/channels and decision makers.
sow_exposure.Required_SOW_Language: Define objective acceptance criteria for routing, channels, carrier failover, integrations, WEM, AI, reporting, performance, data reconciliation, cutover and rollback; prohibit silent/deemed acceptance for unresolved severity-1/2 defects.
sow_exposure.Typical_Assumption_or_Exclusion: A configured flow or successful demo is assumed to constitute acceptance without production-representative failure, capacity and recovery testing.
sow_exposure.Vendor_or_SI_Responsibility: Vendor/SI supports test execution, defect remediation and rollback runbooks for in-scope components.

sow_exposure.Acceptance_Criterion: Named owners can execute routine changes, diagnose common failures and run release/AI regression process before hypercare exit.
sow_exposure.Customer_Responsibility: Assign named Day-2 owners and make them available for design and knowledge transfer.
sow_exposure.Required_SOW_Language: Define role-based training, runbooks, admin ownership, escalation, release/deprecation governance, regression cadence and post-go-live hypercare/knowledge transfer.
sow_exposure.Typical_Assumption_or_Exclusion: Platform training is assumed to equal operational readiness for administrators, WFM/QM leaders, developers, AI owners and support teams.
sow_exposure.Vendor_or_SI_Responsibility: Genesys/SI provides contracted enablement and handoff; customer owns staffing and operational adoption unless otherwise scoped.

sow_exposure.Acceptance_Criterion: Three-layer TCO sensitivity stays within approved thresholds under base, peak and AI-growth scenarios; exit obligations and export paths are contractually clear.
sow_exposure.Customer_Responsibility: Provide demand/seasonality, growth, AI adoption, telephony, integration and staffing assumptions.
sow_exposure.Required_SOW_Language: Attach SKU/BOM, named/concurrent/hourly assumptions, AI token and fair-use rates, telephony/third-party/services costs, price-change rules, ramp/true-down, renewal caps, termination, export and transition assistance.
sow_exposure.Typical_Assumption_or_Exclusion: Seat price is assumed to represent full run-rate cost and public terms are assumed to include buyer-specific ramp, true-down, renewal and exit protections.
sow_exposure.Vendor_or_SI_Responsibility: Genesys/reseller supplies commercial model and usage units; buyer validates scenarios and negotiates protections.

decision_intelligence.Statement: The buyer wants CCaaS, forecasting/scheduling, QM and analytics in one operational data/control plane.

proof_requirements.Reference_Call_Question: For a comparable right-sized deployment, what work remained after go-live that your customer expected to be business-admin owned?
proof_requirements.Required_Test_Data_or_Preconditions: Buyer-approved MVP use cases, user/queue/channel counts and target go-live window.
proof_requirements.Risk_or_Hypothesis: Enterprise breadth will create more implementation/admin burden than value for the proposed scope.
proof_requirements.Success_Criterion: Required outcomes are met with agreed number of admin roles, change steps and services hours inside TTV/TCO threshold.

proof_requirements.Buyer_Controlled_Scenario: Run buyer peak/burst profile at required concurrency/CPS/agent-evaluation rate and WFM topology, including required headroom and any proposed quota increase.

proof_requirements.Failure_Criterion: Rate limit, campaign/WFM limit or increase lead time violates launch/headroom requirement.
proof_requirements.Reference_Call_Question: What production peak did you prove beyond our required profile, and what happened when a quota was approached or exceeded?

proof_requirements.Risk_or_Hypothesis: Peak routing/outbound/WFM load may hit explicit platform limits even while the service is available.
proof_requirements.Success_Criterion: Peak plus buyer headroom completes without throttling/queueing outside thresholds; quota increase and monitoring ownership documented.

proof_requirements.Buyer_Controlled_Scenario: Execute representative voice/digital campaigns with compliance rules, suppression, callbacks and peak concurrency.
proof_requirements.Evidence_to_Capture: Campaign telemetry, CPS/concurrency, contact results, queue effects and exception logs.
proof_requirements.Failure_Criterion: Required campaign count/CPS/contact-rate cannot be met without redesign or unapproved increase.
proof_requirements.Reference_Call_Question: At comparable scale, which outbound limits required redesign or a support increase request?
proof_requirements.Required_Test_Data_or_Preconditions: Real campaign mix, dialing windows, lists and compliance policy.
proof_requirements.Risk_or_Hypothesis: Outbound concurrency/CPS and digital/skills campaign limits could constrain the proposed operating model.
proof_requirements.Success_Criterion: Campaigns sustain target contact rate and compliance behavior without documented-limit breach.

proof_requirements.Buyer_Controlled_Scenario: Model buyer's full WFM hierarchy and peak offered-interaction volumes; run forecast/schedule and cross-unit reporting scenarios.

proof_requirements.Failure_Criterion: Required hierarchy/volume exceeds supported limits or forces unacceptable operating redesign.

proof_requirements.Success_Criterion: Topology and demand remain within supported configuration with acceptable forecast/schedule/reporting performance.

proof_requirements.Risk_or_Hypothesis: Co-built Salesforce integration may still create routing/state/support ambiguity.
proof_requirements.Success_Criterion: Authoritative state remains clear; failed actions are visible/retriable; no duplicate/lost work; incident owner is deterministic.

proof_requirements.Buyer_Controlled_Scenario: Inject timeout/error during work-item assignment, context transfer and action completion; verify recovery and authoritative ownership.

proof_requirements.Failure_Criterion: Failure leaves ambiguous work ownership or unrecoverable state.

proof_requirements.Risk_or_Hypothesis: Co-built ServiceNow integration may still create dual-control-plane state and support risk.
proof_requirements.Success_Criterion: No stranded/duplicated work; state reconciliation and support RACI meet target.

proof_requirements.Buyer_Controlled_Scenario: Inject timeout, 429/rate-limit, malformed response and duplicate/retry conditions into a critical data action.

proof_requirements.Failure_Criterion: Silent failure, duplicate transaction, unbounded retry or ambiguous incident ownership.
proof_requirements.Reference_Call_Question: What custom integration failure produced the largest operational incident, and what observability/control was added afterward?

proof_requirements.Risk_or_Hypothesis: Custom API/data-action integration can fail through timeout, throttling, schema drift or duplicate action.
proof_requirements.Success_Criterion: Failure is detected; customer-safe fallback occurs; retries do not duplicate transactions; alert and owner are clear.

proof_requirements.Buyer_Controlled_Scenario: Use adversarial/wrong-intent cases against a tool-enabled agent: unauthorized request, ambiguous identity, backend timeout, duplicate action, policy conflict and human escalation.

proof_requirements.Failure_Criterion: Unsafe action, missing audit trail, unrecoverable transaction or bad human handoff.

proof_requirements.Risk_or_Hypothesis: Agentic virtual-agent actions may be technically possible without safe authority, rollback or escalation.
